forces.title: Massive AI-driven capital expenditure fuels enterprise device demand
forces.description: Hyperscalers are planning $800 billion in 2026 and $1 trillion in 2027 for AI infrastructure, with a cumulative $2.7 trillion in data center capital expenditures required by 2030. This unprecedented investment is concentrated in data centers and AI compute, directly translating into robust demand for servers, storage, networking, and other enterprise IT hardware, creating a significant and sustained tailwind for Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Elevated semiconductor prices increase cost burden for enterprise hardware
forces.description: The intensified supply-demand imbalance for leading-edge chips (7nm or less) and memory, especially DRAM and HBM, is driving average selling prices (ASPs) well above historical patterns. DRAM prices have risen sixfold since early 2023. This limited supply and high cost for critical inputs will likely persist for 3-5 years, increasing manufacturing costs for enterprise IT hardware and potentially impacting their profitability and affordability for end-customers.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Geopolitical risks threaten global supply of critical chips for AI compute
forces.description: Over 90% of leading-edge chips, crucial for the AI compute sector, are produced in Taiwan. This concentration creates a significant vulnerability to potential disruptions arising from geopolitical tensions, such as those concerning the Taiwan Strait. Any major disruption would severely impact the availability and cost of essential components for servers, storage, and other enterprise devices globally, posing a substantial risk to the Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices sector.

forces.title: Energy availability and cost challenges impede data center expansion in Europe
forces.description: AI data centers are highly energy-intensive, and the rapid build-out requires significant power solutions. While other regions like China and the Middle East are expected to overcome power constraints, Europe may lag due to challenges in energy availability and affordability. This could constrain the expansion of data centers within Europe, thereby limiting demand for enterprise IT hardware in the region.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Growing demand for specialized data center services supports hardware ecosystem
forces.description: As data center ownership becomes more capital-intensive and crowded, there is increasing investment in capabilities critical to data center build, deliverability, and maintenance. This includes services such as networking, commissioning, cooling systems, and power integration. Companies involved in providing these specialized services for data center infrastructure can capture AI-driven growth, indirectly benefiting the Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices sector by enabling more efficient and complex deployments.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Global push for data sovereignty drives demand for local AI compute infrastructure
forces.description: Governments worldwide are increasingly seeking domestically located and controlled AI training and computing power capacity to meet security, data residency, and regulatory requirements. This creates a distinct demand for enterprise IT hardware that can be deployed within national borders, often through local operators, partnerships, or joint ventures. This trend generates new opportunities for European Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices providers to serve national strategic interests and secure data.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Data center liquid cooling systems see surge in demand
forces.description: The growing intensity of AI compute in data centers necessitates advanced cooling solutions. Liquid-cooling systems, requiring highly engineered components such as cold plates, cooling distribution units, and manifolds, are experiencing a significant increase in demand. This creates a specific tailwind for manufacturers of these specialized components, which are integral parts of the broader enterprise hardware ecosystem supporting high-performance data centers.

forces.title: Robust M&A activity in digital infrastructure signals growth confidence
forces.description: Global digital infrastructure M&A deals increased by over 60% in 2025, with data center transaction value growing significantly (e.g., threefold in the US from 2024 to 2025). This strong investor appetite and consolidation in data centers and hyperscale-adjacent platforms indicate high confidence and significant capital allocation to the underlying infrastructure. This environment fosters expansion and upgrades, driving demand for enterprise IT hardware.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: AI accelerates demand for higher-value, advanced semiconductor components
forces.description: The rise of AI is fundamentally altering semiconductor industry economics by accelerating a shift towards higher-value leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This change goes beyond mere volume increases, emphasizing advanced specifications and performance critical for AI workloads. This structural shift drives enterprise hardware manufacturers to integrate more sophisticated and higher-priced components, influencing product design, cost structures, and competitive differentiation within the Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices sector.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Orbital data centers emerge as complementary layer for specific AI workloads
forces.description: Space-based data centers are becoming technically feasible at scale within 5-10 years, driven by specific orbit-advantaged AI workloads such as sovereign data processing and space-generated data analysis. While they carry a cost premium compared to terrestrial infrastructure, they are expected to capture 10-15% of the global AI data center market by 2040. This structural shift introduces a new deployment environment for enterprise compute hardware, requiring specialized, radiation-hardened components.
forces.source_title: Space-Based Data Centers: More Than Hype, but Not a Revolution

forces.title: Irish electronics sector faces restructuring and cost-cutting pressure
forces.description: The Irish electronics sector is experiencing industry-wide restructuring and cost-cutting initiatives, including workforce reductions among major global players. This reflects a heightened focus on efficiency and margin protection amidst challenging global conditions, such as inventory corrections and shifting demand patterns within the semiconductor supply chain. This trend creates pressure on Irish suppliers within the Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices sector to optimize operations and manage costs effectively.

viewpoints.title: AI-driven data center build-out to propel semiconductor market to $2.3 trillion by 2030
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects the semiconductor market will reach $2.3 trillion by 2030, a 44% increase from previous estimates, primarily fueled by unprecedented AI infrastructure investments by hyperscalers. This surge is driven by high average selling prices for leading-edge chips and memory due to persistent supply-demand imbalance in data center expansion. Companies underestimating this opportunity based on modest $1 trillion projections risk missing significant value creation for underlying hardware.
viewpoints.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

viewpoints.title: Irish electronics sector faces global headwinds but remains strategically important
viewpoints.description: The Irish electronics sector benefits from strong foreign direct investment and its strategic position in high-value activities, including those supporting enterprise hardware. However, it navigates a challenging global environment marked by inventory corrections, shifting demand, and profitability pressure across the semiconductor supply chain. Despite these industry-wide restructuring and cost-cutting initiatives, the sector is well-positioned to benefit from long-term technology and innovation trends.

demand_drivers.description: Hyperscalers are allocating massive capital expenditures (approx. $800B in 2026, $1T in 2027) towards AI infrastructure, driving demand for chips used in servers and data centers.
Surging demand for leading-edge chips and memory is largely due to the expansion and proliferation of data centers globally.

pnl_drivers.description: Intensifying supply-demand imbalance for leading-edge chips and memory, especially DRAM and HBM, pushes ASPs well above predicted levels, driving revenue growth for chip sales destined for enterprise devices.

market_sizing.methodology: Represents chip sales for servers and data centers, expected to rise to $1.2 trillion by 2030. Methodology based on comprehensive analysis of fabless companies, OEMs with in-house design, and captive-chip players, incorporating detailed data, leading to higher estimates than other analysts.

demand_drivers.description: AI applications not requiring real-time response, such as batch processing, enterprise back-office AI, and scientific inference, can leverage orbital compute without impacting user experience.

Processing nationally sensitive or regulated data that must not transit foreign networks or jurisdictions, driven by government AI services and critical systems backup requiring secure, remote hardware.
Co-locating compute directly with data sources in orbit for applications like Earth observation, climate monitoring, and disaster response, necessitating specialized enterprise hardware.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected annual revenue captured by space-based data centers, estimated to be 10% to 15% of the global AI data center market by 2040 (range $240 billion to $320 billion). The lower bound is used for 'tam_value'.
